video_title: How to Survive a Flood, According to Science

segments.text:
Floods wreak havoc all over the world, causing terrible damage to homes, ruining infrastructure, drowning people, and spreading disease 
after the flooding stops. What do you need to know to stay safe? Well, here's how you can survive a flood, Before a flood, prepare for the worst
situation that could possibly happen.

This includes bottled water, a battery-operated radio, freshly-charged batteries, and bug spray. When a flood begins,  you wont have time to go shopping, so if heavy rains or flooding are expected, listen to the radio, so you'll be able to hear
warnings from the government. A "flood watch" means that 
a flood could happen, but there's no danger yet. A "flood warning" means the flood
has started or will start soon. A flash flood is really dangerous, because it happens so fast. If there's any chance of a flash flood, start preparing right away. Second, if you live near ground level,

That includes your laptop, important papers, TVs, and any pets that can't move by themselves like fish in an aquarium,
or birds in a cage. If you don't have a higher floor, identify the most important things and be ready to take them to a safe place, like the home of a friend or family member.

If you don't, your home could be damaged by electrical fires, or you could endanger yourself 
or your loved ones with possible electrocution.

During a flood, tap water could be
turned off or contaminated. You could get extremely sick from
drinking contaminated water, so be sure to pack several 
bottles and keep them with you.

Unlike people, insects love floods. In fact, bugs breed very quickly in the
still water that's left over after flooding.  Wouldn't it be terrible to survive the flood only to get a dangerous 
disease from infected mosquitos?

If news sources tell you to evacuate, leave your home and move to higher ground. Once the flood comes, you'll need to avoid low places like
basements and ditches. The danger of drowning is very real, and the higher up you get,
the safer you'll be.

If you're wet or standing in water, touching electricity can be fatal. And if you're dry, the equipment itself
might be wet, so it's best to stay away. Before a flood, you can certainly
drive to higher ground in your car. Once a flood comes, however, that's a very dangerous thing to do. If water rushes around your car, forget how much you paid 
and how nice the leather interiors are, abandon your car and run to higher ground. The weight of the water can prevent you
from opening the doors. Don't risk getting trapped inside. If you can find a stick, it's a good idea to check the firmness 
of the ground you're about to walk on. Try to avoid walking through water if possible, because moving water can sweep you away, or downed power lines could electrocute you. So, the rains have stopped and
the flood waters have stopped rising. Are you finally safe? Unfortunately, the answer is no. After a flood, there will be water everywhere that's contaminated with anything
from oil and raw sewage to diseases. Or, the water could be electrically charged. Avoid the water. Beware of water-damaged roads and bridges, as they could collapse under a car's weight. When you return home, be sure to disinfect anything that was
in contact with flood waters. Otherwise, you or your loved ones
could get really sick. Floods are dangerous both 
during and after they happen, so it's best to be ready, especially if you live 
near a large body of water. You never know when a rainstorm
can turn into a flood. However, if you follow the tips in this video, you have a good chance 
of surviving a flood, According to Science.
